PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
REDLINE REVIEW MEMORANDUM
Energy Natural Resources — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Concession Agreement

Matter: MATTER FILE 13 — Energy Natural Resources
Re: TxDOT Concession Agreement — Redline Review of Counterparty Markup
Prepared by: [Assigned Counsel], Harrow & Vane LLP
Date: [DATE]

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have reviewed the Texas Department of Transportation ("TxDOT") counterparty markup of the Concession Agreement against (i) our original draft, (ii) the firm's negotiation playbook and base materials for this matter, (iii) the closing-context lender and surety letters, and (iv) the financial model. The TxDOT markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three material deviations, each of which requires reconciliation against the scheduled exceptions and the deal team's controlling negotiation instructions:

1. Indemnification Cap and Basket Structure. TxDOT silently reduces the indemnification cap and converts the basket from a true deductible to a tipping basket.
2. Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") Definition. TxDOT adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.
3. Survival / Limitation Period. TxDOT introduces a new, shortened limitation period that truncates survival for the core representations, directly contradicting Exhibit B and the survival matrix.

Consistent with the controlling partner instruction (the latest message in the matter correspondence thread), the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Accordingly, our recommended posture is to (a) accept the basket conversion on the client-approved terms while preserving the indemnification cap, (b) resist the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs which are not supported by the scheduled disclosures, and (c) reject, as a walk-away point, any shortening of the survival period for the core representations.

Risk summary: Two of the three deviations are moderate-risk, commercially resolvable items; the survival-period reduction is a HIGH-severity, walk-away issue that we must not concede.

II. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE

A. Parties and Instrument. This matter concerns a concession agreement between the client (the Concessionaire side) and the Texas Department of Transportation ("TxDOT"), covering the development, financing, construction, and operation of a toll/transportation concession. The operative agreement contains representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions, together with the disclosure schedules and exhibits (including Exhibit B setting the survival matrix).

B. Materials Reviewed. The review was performed against the matter's operative file, comprising:
- Original Concession Agreement draft and the firm's negotiation playbook / base position on indemnity, MAE, and survival terms;
- TxDOT counterparty markup (the deviations under review);
- Disclosure Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and Exhibit B;
- Lender and surety letters bearing on financing, security, and performance-bond underpinning of the concession obligations;
- The financial model used to size the concession economics, indemnity exposure, and risk.

C. Controlling Instructions. The deal correspondence is controlling on negotiation priorities. The latest (controlling) message provides that the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stated the opposite priority ordering and are superseded; only the latest message controls. The deliverable reflects the controlling instruction.

III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS WITH RISK RATINGS AND COUNTER-PROPOSAL LANGUAGE

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap and Basket Conversion (from Deductible to Tipping Basket)

Original Draft / Playbook Position. Our original draft and the firm's playbook provide for a hard indemnification cap (a fixed ceiling on aggregate indemnity exposure) and a deductible basket: losses are recoverable only to the extent they exceed the deductible threshold. The playbook treats a true deductible as the standard; conversion of the basket to a "tipping" (first-dollar) structure is a deviation from standard practice.

TxDOT Markup. The markup (i) silently reduces the value of the indemnification cap and (ii) converts the basket from a deductible into a tipping basket, meaning that once the threshold is crossed, TxDOT would recover from dollar one (first-dollar coverage) rather than only the excess over the deductible.

Cross-Reference — Schedules. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift to the client. Because the scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, the cap reduction and basket conversion must be quantified against the retained liabilities disclosed in Schedule 5.2 and the financial model's sizing of indemnity exposure.

Cross-Reference — Lender and Surety Letters. The lender and surety letters contemplate a defined cap and deductible structure supporting the financing and the performance/security package. A silent cap reduction and conversion to a tipping basket would alter the risk allocation underpinning the lenders' and sureties' underwriting, and could be inconsistent with the closure of the financing conditions.

Risk Rating: MODERATE. The basket conversion is conceded by the client under the controlling instruction; the cap reduction remains a real economic risk, but is commercially resolvable through negotiation of the cap level.

Controlling Instruction. Client will concede the basket conversion. It does not authorize a reduction of the indemnification cap.

Recommended Position:
- Concede the conversion to a tipping basket, but on the express condition that the indemnification cap remain at the level set in the original draft.
- Reject any reduction of the indemnification cap.
- Quantify the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability exposure against the proposed cap to ensure no silent shift occurs.

Counter-Proposal Language:
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in Section [__], the Parties agree that indemnification claims shall be recoverable on a first-dollar basis once the aggregate amount of Losses has exceeded the Basket (the 'Basket' being a tipping basket), provided that the aggregate liability of the Concessionaire under this Section [__] shall in no event exceed [ORIGINAL CAP AMOUNT]. For the avoidance of doubt, the conversion of the Basket to a tipping basket does not modify, reduce, or otherwise alter the indemnification cap set forth in this Section [__], and any retained liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2 remain subject to the Indemnification Cap in full."

DEVIATION 2 — Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") Definition — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs

Original Draft / Playbook Position. Our original draft defines "Material Adverse Effect" using the standard formulation, with customary carve-outs. The playbook treats broad, read-into-MAE regulatory carve-outs as contrary to market practice where regulatory exposure is a known matter already disclosed.

TxDOT Markup. The markup adds carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter — that is, the pending regulatory inquiries and regulatory-action risk bearing directly on the concession.

Cross-Reference — Schedules. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect precisely with the new MAE carve-outs. Because the scheduled exceptions control over general statements, the carve-outs would operate to strip the client of MAE protection for the very matters already disclosed and known to TxDOT, and could be read to permit TxDOT to walk away without liability where the disclosed inquiries mature into adverse regulatory outcomes.

Cross-Reference — Lender and Surety Letters. The lender and surety support the concession on the basis of the MAE / representation guardrails. Broad regulatory-action carve-outs would undermine the condition-precedent protections that the financing and surety packages rely upon.

Risk Rating: MODERATE-TO-HIGH. The carve-outs target the exact regulatory risk at issue in this matter and, if combined with the pending inquiries in Schedule 3.7, could erode a central risk-allocation protection. This is not a conceded item.

Recommended Position:
- Reject the addition of MAE carve-outs for regulatory action, particularly where the underlying regulatory matters are already the subject of disclosure in Schedule 3.7.
- If TxDOT insists, limit any carve-out to regulatory action not arising from the disclosed inquiries, and require that the carve-out not capture matters disclosed in Schedule 3.7.

Counter-Proposal Language:
"The definition of 'Material Adverse Effect' shall not exclude, and no MAE shall be deemed not to have occurred by reason of, any effect, change, event or development arising from or relating to any Regulatory Action (as defined in Schedule 3.7), including any inquiry, investigation, notice, audit, or enforcement action relating to the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7. For the avoidance of doubt, any Regulatory Action relating to or arising out of the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7 shall be deemed to constitute a Material Adverse Effect to the fullest extent otherwise provided herein and shall not be carved out of this definition."

DEVIATION 3 — Survival / Limitation Period Reduction for Core Representations

Original Draft / Playbook Position. Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the representations and warranties. The core representations survive for the periods set forth in Exhibit B (the firm-standard survival periods). The playbook treats any shortening of the core-representation survival period as a departure from the approved matrix.

TxDOT Markup. The markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival for the core representations, directly contradicting Exhibit B and the survival matrix. Under the controlling deal instruction, the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.

Cross-Reference — Schedules. Exhibit B controls the survival matrix, and scheduled exceptions control over any general statements. The markup's limitation-period change contradicts Exhibit B and therefore must not be accepted.

Cross-Reference — Lender and Surety Letters. The lender and surety letters assume the survival periods in Exhibit B remain intact for the purposes of the underlying representations and covenants that the financing and surety collateralize. Shortening survival would reduce the term over which the client could pursue recovery for misrepresentations and covenant breaches, undermining the risk allocation integral to the financing.

Risk Rating: HIGH — WALK-AWAY. Any survival-period reduction for the core representations is a deal-breaker under the controlling instruction and must not be conceded.

Recommended Position:
- Refuse to accept any reduction in the survival period for the core representations.
- Hold Exhibit B as controlling.
- Escalate and, absent TxDOT's withdrawal of the change, treat this as a walk-away item.

Counter-Proposal Language:
"The survival of the representations and warranties set forth in Section [__] shall be governed exclusively by the survival matrix set forth on Exhibit B, which is incorporated herein by reference and shall control notwithstanding any inconsistent or contrary provision in this Agreement or any exhibit, schedule, or other writing. No limitation period set forth herein shall shorten, reduce, or otherwise modify the survival periods for the core representations established on Exhibit B. The Parties agree that [Insert any requested non-core adjustment] does not apply to, and shall not be construed to reduce, the survival of the core representations."

IV. CROSS-REFERENCE TO FINANCIAL MODEL AND LENDER/SUREY LETTERS

A. Financial Model. The financial model sizes the concession economics and the indemnity exposure associated with the disclosed retained liabilities (Schedule 5.2) and the pending regulatory inquiries (Schedule 3.7). Our analysis confirms:
- The cap-reduction delta under Deviation 1, when measured against the retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2, produces a meaningful increase in the client's unindemnified exposure if conceded. The tipping-basket conversion, while conceded, must not be accompanied by a cap reduction, or the financial model's assumed exposure ceiling would be exceeded.
- The MAE regulatory carve-outs (Deviation 2) would, if read with Schedule 3.7, remove the risk allocation that the financial model assumes for the two pending inquiries.
- The survival shortening (Deviation 3) would truncate the recovery window over which the financial model assumes recourse for core breaches, in each case altering the deal risk profile on terms not reflected in the model.

B. Lender Letters. The lender letters condition financing on the maintenance of the indemnification cap and survival protections as drafted. The cap reduction and survival shortening would be inconsistent with the lenders' underwriting and could jeopardize the effectiveness of conditions precedent to the financing. We recommend flagging Deviations 1 (cap element) and 3 to the lender working group.

C. Surety Letters. The surety letters support the performance/security package. The indemnification changes and MAE carve-outs would alter the risk profile the surety relied upon. The retention of the true cap (Deviation 1) and the rejection of the MAE carve-outs (Deviation 2) are necessary to preserve consistency with the surety's issuance.

V. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATION POSTURE AND SCRIPT

Consistent with the controlling instruction and the analysis above:

1. Basket Conversion — CONCEDE, conditioned on preservation of the indemnification cap (Deviation 1).
2. Indemnification Cap Reduction — REJECT. Offer the counter-proposal language in Section III (Deviation 1).
3. MAE Regulatory Carve-Outs — REJECT / RE-CARVE. Offer the counter-proposal language in Section III (Deviation 2), limiting any carve-out away from Schedule 3.7 matters.
4. Survival Reduction — WALK-AWAY. Reject outright; hold Exhibit B. Do not offer any competing term that shortens core representation survival. Escalate per the deal instruction if TxDOT does not withdraw.

VI. RISK RATING SUMMARY TABLE

Deviation | Description | Risk Rating | Recommended Action
1 | Indemnification cap reduction + basket conversion to tipping | MODERATE (cap) / LOW (basket concession) | Concede basket; reject cap reduction; counter-proposal per Section III
2 | MAE regulatory-action carve-outs | MODERATE-TO-HIGH | Reject / re-carve per Section III; preserve Schedule 3.7 scope
3 | Survival-period reduction for core representations | HIGH — WALK-AWAY | Reject, hold Exhibit B; escalate; do not concede

VII. NEXT STEPS

1. Circulate this memorandum to the deal team with the risk-rating summary.
2. Quantify the Deviation 1 cap delta in dollars against the financial model and Schedule 5.2 before responding to TxDOT.
3. Confirm lender and surety positions on Deviations 1 and 3 with the working groups.
4. Respond to TxDOT with the counter-proposal language set forth in Section III, withholding Deviation 3 as a walk-away item.
